_comment: Canonical implementation-language registry. Every Build lesson ships code in each language with ci=true; the learner picks one in start-learning and the tutor teaches in it. `dir` is the folder under code/, `run`/`test` are the canonical commands executed from inside that folder, `entry` names the file the tutor walks through first. Add a language by adding an entry and a code/<dir>/ folder to each lesson; scripts/run_lesson.py and scripts/project_test.py read this file. Java and Python are complete (ci=true). Go is registered with ci=false until its port is complete; a lesson is Complete when every ci=true language is present.

languages.name: Java
languages.why: Records, sealed interfaces, and pattern matching make state machines and money types explicit. The JVM memory model is the reference point for every concurrency lesson.

languages.name: Python
languages.why: The shortest distance from an idea to running code. The GIL and Decimal module are teaching tools in their own right.

languages.name: Go
languages.why: Goroutines, channels, and context make distributed-systems lessons concrete, and the toolchain ships its own test runner and race detector.
